## 固定收益開場論點

6月30日收盤時，前一交易日由前端主導的重新定價，已擴大為整條美債殖利率曲線的賣壓。10年期殖利率收於4.44%，上升6個基點，其中實質殖利率升至2.20%，貢獻4個基點。市場解讀出現邊際變化：勞動需求展現韌性、消費者信心轉強，加上股市風險偏好旺盛，長存續期間需求及能源壓力緩解已不足以支撐中期美債。通膨補償也同步上升，因此收盤同時反映更高的實質利率門檻，以及通膨風險小幅回升。

美國數據是第1條傳導管道。5月職缺高於預期，也略高於4月修正後水準，顯示勞動需求尚未明確轉弱。消費者信心改善，但家庭對就業市場的評估惡化。德州服務業調查則顯示，營收與就業加速，投入成本、薪資及售價也同步上升。這組數據讓聯準會有空間維持限制性政策，並促使市場重新評估今年稍後再度升息的可能性。不過，房價轉弱、信心調查內部訊號不一，意味數據尚未構成明確的景氣加速訊號。

全球債市呈現明顯反向訊號，卻未能扭轉美債跌勢。油價走低帶動德國與法國通膨降幅超出預期，降低歐洲央行連續升息的迫切性。日本走勢則相反：2年期公債標售需求強勁，超長端卻大幅走弱。財政擴張、日圓極度疲弱，加上市場質疑日本央行政策正常化速度，推高長期通膨與供給風險補償。跨市場訊號因而呈現能源價格帶動通膨降溫，但實質利率與主權債期限溢價壓力持續並存。

信用市場整體仍可順利融資，但資金承接更具選擇性。日本企業單季外幣發債規模創新高，新興市場國際債券上半年發行額也刷新紀錄。另一方面，Sable Offshore大幅縮減槓桿貸款規模、中國限制高成本境外借款，以及市場日益關注AI債務的期限錯配，則凸顯融資管道最薄弱之處。因此，本交易日呈現風險偏好升溫、實質殖利率上升且初級市場仍正常運作的格局，而非流動性全面撤出。尚待釐清的核心問題是：當勞動需求、資本支出及資產價格維持強勁時，能源價格走低能否持續約束通膨預期。

## 美債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與殖利率曲線結構

美債各年期普遍下跌，指標年期附近壓力最大。2年期殖利率上升4個基點至4.14%，5年期上升5個基點至4.19%，10年期上升6個基點至4.44%，30年期則上升5個基點至4.91%。週一的溫和熊市趨平，轉為截至10年期的溫和熊市趨陡。限制性政策仍牽制前端，但成長展望轉強、避險需求下降，使調整延伸至中段與長端。

殖利率曲線斜率反映領跌部位已經改變。2s10s利差擴大2個基點至30個基點，2s30s擴大1個基點至77個基點。5年期相對兩翼仍偏貴，2s5s10s蝶式利差維持在-20個基點。10年期表現落後於前端與長債的平均表現，使2s10s30s蝶式利差上升3個基點至-17個基點。變動幅度雖有限，仍顯示本交易日並非2年期部位的機械式反轉。

拉長至1個月觀察，近期政策壓力與遠端存續期間支撐仍然分明。2年期殖利率累計上升16個基點，5年期上升6個基點；10年期下降1個基點，30年期下降8個基點。儘管聯準會立場轉鷹推升前端，6月油價回落與通膨預期下降，仍保住長天期債券的部分漲幅。週二賣壓縮小這項分歧，但未將其消除。投資人當日提高持有存續期間所要求的補償，對政策路徑及超長端市場出清利率的月度判斷則仍明顯不同。

通膨連結債市場顯示，10年期名目殖利率上升6個基點，同時來自實質利率與通膨補償。10年期實質殖利率上升4個基點至2.20%，損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點至2.24%。5年期實質殖利率上升3個基點至1.93%，7年期上升4個基點至2.06%，20年期與30年期則各上升5個基點，分別至2.54%及2.73%。各年期實質殖利率同步上揚，顯示名目債券賣壓主要源自更高的成長與政策門檻，通膨風險的影響相對較小。

5月職缺是本交易日最明確的催化因素。職缺增至759萬個，略高於4月修正後水準，也高於市場預期。近期非農就業增幅回升後，這項數據顯示勞動需求仍然穩定，因而壓低美債價格。美國經濟評議會6月消費者信心指數也小幅上升，進一步反映總需求仍具韌性。不過，勞動市場細項較不樂觀：消費者對就業情勢的評估惡化，對後續改善的期待也有限。因此，數據雖削弱政策即將轉鬆的理由，卻未證明勞動市場全面轉強。

區域與房市數據使聯準會政策訊號維持雙向。達拉斯聯準銀行德州服務業營收指數由5.0升至9.8，就業指數由-3.2升至8.1，整體商業活動指數由-7.7升至2.9。投入價格指數由29.7升至36.5，薪資與福利由6.2升至15.3，售價則由5.0升至7.7。相較之下，美國聯邦住房金融局4月房價指數下跌0.1%，年增率放緩至2.0%，減弱房價通膨與擔保品價值所釋出的偏強訊號。

即使油價已自戰時高點崩跌，市場仍持續預期聯準會下半年至少升息1次，週二公布的數據更強化這項限制性解讀。殖利率曲線並未反映能源衝擊單純重演：原油當日下跌，10年期殖利率升幅又大多來自實質殖利率。更合理的解讀是，勞動需求與支出維持韌性，AI相關投資也可能增添另一條需求與通膨管道，因此政策或須維持緊縮。房市轉弱及消費者對勞動市場的觀感惡化，仍是可信的反向證據。

國庫券殖利率曲線反映局部季底壓力，而非全面現金緊縮。4週期票息等值殖利率下降2個基點至3.67%，6週期上升5個基點至3.73%，8週期維持在3.73%。13週及17週期殖利率分別維持在3.83%及3.88%，26週及52週期則各上升1個基點，分別至3.98%及3.97%。單日最大變動集中在6週期，新供給與假期融資窗口使市場焦點集中於此。

美國財政部標售$800億、42天期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.655%，投標倍數為2.71。間接投標人取得競爭性得標額的69.01%，直接投標人取得4.96%，交易商承接比例為26.03%；按最高利率獲配的比率為54.61%。發行及交割日為7月2日，因此週二的投標結果與隨後的現金移轉分屬不同時點。此次標售顯示季底供給獲得承接，但6週期現券殖利率同時上升，融資環境並不像最短期國庫券所顯示的那樣全面寬鬆。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

上市信用資產的報酬顯示，高評級長存續期間資產比低評級風險資產更明顯受到美債賣壓拖累。LQD下跌0.5743%，HYG下跌0.0500%，JNK下跌0.0311%。股市走強、波動率下降，使投機級債券基金接近持平；指標殖利率上升則拖累存續期間較長的投資級債券基金。整體風險偏好依然穩定，主要拖累來自存續期間。至於信用取得是否真正受限，仍須觀察個別發行條件與融資結構。

日本發行人展現極強的美元市場融資能力。Mizuho Financial Group與Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group本週初完成近$100億債券定價，使日本企業單季外幣發債規模增至約$540億。此一總額較1年前增加逾80%，也是自1999年有資料以來首度單季超過$500億。Panasonic週二也啟動另一筆美元債發行。日圓疲弱可提高資金換回日圓後的國內所得，本地利率上升則使企業在收購及擴張時更重視境外融資。

Sable Offshore則位於承接光譜的另一端。市場對一筆固定利率15%的槓桿貸款需求有限，規模由原訂$10億縮減至$6.75億；即使發行價僅為面額的97美分，到期年限也只有2.5年，仍未獲足額承接。公司另尋求透過股票及可轉換公司債籌措$4億，可轉債票息最高達6.5%，轉換溢價為30%至35%。其股價一度下跌55%，反映近期到期負債帶來的股權稀釋與再融資成本。

Sable原擬以這筆融資償還Exxon Mobil定期貸款。該貸款先前已支付$3,000萬展期費用，修訂後的展期期限至7月31日。攤還獎勵條款可能在貸款存續期間逐步降低餘額，但公司重啟加州外海營運所涉及的訴訟，仍使現金流能見度受到干擾。槓桿融資市場整體需求雖然強勁，面對同時具有執行風險、時程緊迫及票息異常高昂的借款人，仍未提供足額承接。

中國收緊高成本境外再融資的界線。國家發展和改革委員會要求部分銀行業者避免承銷殖利率高於4%的境外人民幣債券，以及殖利率高於5%的美元債券，尤其是地方政府融資平台所發行的債券。地方政府融資平台約有$1,170億境外債券流通在外；中國企業在2026年剩餘期間約有$710億債務到期，明年到期規模更超過$1,300億。部分額度已遭削減10%至20%，迫使至少1家國有借款人轉向成本較高的短期銀行融資。

私募市場也出現相關的流動性斷層。主要另類資產管理公司的贖回要求增加，規模$1.8兆的私募信貸市場部分領域流動性流失之際，Len Tannenbaum正為一檔新基金募資。他認為，小型軟體公司尤其可能在1年內遭遇再融資困難，但具有實際現金流的中型市場下緣借款人仍可取得資金。這項分歧顯示，龐大的私募資本池可以和更嚴格的契約條款、更高的利差同時存在，尤其是在AI顛覆降低獲利能見度的領域。

AI融資也為信用市場帶來期限錯配。IMF資本市場主管Tobias Adrian關注的是，超大規模雲端業者發行中長期債務，為晶片及其他折舊速度可能遠快於債務期限的實體資產融資。強勁的獲利能力與實際獲利表現，迄今仍使這波熱潮有別於全面性的估值泡沫。然而，信用風險不容忽視：科技股創紀錄的表現目前可以支撐融資，但未來龐大的資本需求將增加債券供給；若商業化成果不如預期，長天期債權人將承擔風險。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

歐洲通膨數據強化能源帶動的通膨降溫管道。德國6月通膨率由2.7%降至2.4%，低於2.5%的預估中位數。法國由2.8%降至2.0%，市場原預期為2.3%；義大利則放緩至3.1%，經濟學家原先預期不變。西班牙稍早公布的3.6%，仍是主要國別反例。多國通膨同步下降，降低歐洲央行立即再次升息的必要性，也有助解釋油價走低之際，美國損益兩平通膨率為何僅小幅上升。

歐洲央行官員仍認為，政策影響取決於成本向終端價格的轉嫁。Martins Kazaks表示，和平進程壓低能源價格後，連續調整利率的迫切性已大幅下降；Olli Rehn認為未出現顯著的第2輪效應，通膨預期也維持穩定。首席經濟學家Philip Lane則持續關注過去4個月能源成本上升會如何傳導至食品與服務價格。6月升息是2023年以來首次，政策利率升至2.25%。各國通膨數據轉弱，使政策討論轉向耐心觀望，但尚未消除成本後續傳導的風險。

德國勞動數據進一步支持耐心觀望。經季節調整後，6月失業人數僅減少1,000人，BA-X勞動需求指數維持在103。最新估計顯示，社會保險就業人數較1年前減少7.1萬人。勞動需求疲弱，限制能源成本演變為薪資—物價循環的空間，但整體通膨仍高於目標。因此，當前能源通膨下降與勞動市場低迷都對歐洲債券形成支撐，服務與食品價格的轉嫁則仍是主要限制。

英國數據同樣呈現產出有韌性、家庭需求轉弱的分化。第1季實質GDP成長率維持在0.6%，主要由服務業成長0.8%帶動。人均實質家庭可支配所得下降0.8%，儲蓄率由9.6%降至8.9%。剔除特定因素的經常帳赤字縮小至£151億，相當於GDP的1.9%；初次所得赤字縮小的影響，大於貿易逆差擴大。經濟成長使英國公債未能全面上漲，家庭所得與外部收支改善則降低其他英國公債風險。

英格蘭銀行總裁Andrew Bailey強調，油價下降已重新增加政策彈性。他認為，戰爭前市場預期政策利率可由3.75%下調2次，原屬合理。原油先前一度超過$110，目前已跌破$80，也低於英格蘭銀行4月預測所採用的價格路徑。Bailey仍預期通膨將由2.8%升至今年稍後約3.2%，但同時強調成長疲弱及中期政策視野。因此，能源價格帶來的升息迫切性已經下降，英國公債卻尚未獲得明確的近期寬鬆承諾。

日本是本交易日全球主權債市最強的反向力量。30年期日本公債殖利率上升11個基點至3.94%，20年期上升9個基點至3.64%。首相Sanae Takaichi計畫在2040財政年度以前動員超過¥370兆公私部門投資，引發市場對未來發債供給與財政可持續性的疑慮。美元兌日圓升破162，凸顯輸入性通膨，也加深市場疑慮：偏好寬鬆政策的政府是否會允許日本央行以足夠速度推動政策正常化。

日本公債前端則呈現不同走勢。2年期標售投標倍數為4.82，高於前次的3.70及過去12個月平均的3.74。標售尾差由0.02縮窄至0.005，結果公布後2年期殖利率下降1.5個基點。前端殖利率偏高，加上市場預期日本央行將審慎行事，共同支撐需求。這股強勢幾乎無助於緩解長端的財政與通膨風險，反而使殖利率曲線分化更加鮮明。

國內買盤為長端提供部分支撐。殖利率上升後，Meiji Yasuda計畫在截至2027年3月的財政年度買進超過¥2兆超長期日本公債，規模為原計畫的2倍。由Takaichi任命的一位新任日本央行審議委員也表示，通膨常態尚未牢固建立，進一步強化市場對政策將逐步正常化的預期。紐約收盤後，IMF另敦促紐西蘭央行在年底前，將目前2.25%的政策利率調高至以約3%為中心的中性水準，為下一個全球交易時段增添亞太地區的緊縮訊號。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

美國實質殖利率上升，帶動新興市場債券普遍走弱。EMB下跌0.3925%，美元指數當日則近乎持平。相較於美債跌幅，新興市場債整體跌勢溫和，初級市場融資管道也依然極為暢通。新興市場主權及企業上半年發行的美元與歐元計價債券達創紀錄的$4,500億，較1年前增加15%；相對美債的利差縮窄至154個基點，為2007年以來最窄。

強勁的發債活動也使估值面臨更高要求。墨西哥、沙烏地阿拉伯、南韓、波蘭、土耳其及巴西的融資額均超過$100億；新興市場美元債上半年報酬率達2.1%，為美債漲幅的3倍。龐大的全球買盤協助借款人在利差偏窄時提前籌資。週二美國殖利率上升則凸顯另一面的脆弱性：即使廣泛美元指數持穩，債務償付成本與次級市場表現仍可能惡化。

衣索比亞在先前仍陷入僵局的法律與債權人協調程序中取得實質進展。代表約45%之2024年到期債券持有人的委員會證實，各方已就主要重組條款達成初步協議，違約債券延續漲勢至面額的109.17美分。這項協議降低2023年漏付票息後的近期法律執行風險。不過，債權人批評IMF同時擔任優先貸款人及債務可持續性評估者，使共同框架的治理問題仍未解決。回收預期雖然改善，程序風險尚未消失。

國內政策可信度持續吸引資金流入部分亞洲主權債。印尼央行意外緊縮以支撐印尼盾後，截至6月26日，外國投資人淨買進$12億印尼政府債券，為逾1年來最快的單月流入速度。10年期殖利率為7.12%，低於6月稍早的7.47%。印度符合指數資格的政府債券則獲得創紀錄的$42億資金流入，主因油價下降減輕進口負擔；不過，季風偏弱仍可能帶來食品通膨壓力。

拉丁美洲市場選擇性獎勵果斷的政策行動與通膨降溫。法院終止政府阻撓央行召開會議的權力後，哥倫比亞將政策利率上調75個基點至12%。升幅超過多數市場預測，帶動債券與匯率雙雙上漲。波蘭通膨率由3.1%降至2.5%，低於2.7%的預估中位數，使其指標10年期公債殖利率降至3月初以來最低，儘管波蘭茲羅提走弱。智利1年期損益兩平通膨率則在1個月內下降逾100個基點至2.19%，寬鬆預期因而集中於短端。

南非仍處於對通膨較為敏感的一側。未來2年通膨預期由3.6%升至3.9%，高於央行3%的目標；遠期利率協議則反映升息25個基點的機率為88%。南非與波蘭、智利的差異顯示，全球油價回落並未使各國本地利率同步下降。國內通膨預期、食品價格風險及政策機關的反應方式，仍決定能源價格走低能否轉化為較低的主權融資成本。

中國6月官方調查呈現好壞不一的區域需求訊號。製造業指數回升至50.3，重返擴張區間，其中生產為51.4、新訂單為51.2；就業則降至48.5，小型企業指數降至48.2。非製造業活動維持在50.2，營建業仍處於收縮區間，指數為49.0。這些數據小幅支撐商品與出口需求，卻未消除小型借款人的壓力，也使地方政府融資平台境外發債規則收緊所引發的再融資疑慮更加突出。

外資配置顯示，市場改善不只反映在股票與盧比。新德里取消政府債券稅負後，海外投資人6月增持創紀錄的3,980億盧比指數合格印度政府債券，同期卻自股市撤出$31億。債券資金流入直接增加本地存續期間需求，也協助盧比自前1個月接近每美元97盧比的歷史低點回升。油價下跌與稅制調整改善投資條件，但季風偏弱仍可能推升食品通膨，印度央行如何因應也是這項交易的限制。

收盤後稍晚公布的消息，將委內瑞拉列入債務管理風險名單。兩起地震估計造成$67億直接損失；投資人評估這筆財政成本對原已艱難的債務重組有何影響，債券因而下跌。由於消息出現在收盤後，不能用來解釋已完成的美國交易時段。不過，災害支出、稀缺的外部流動性及既有債權人談判相互牽動，仍為下一交易日增添主權損失承擔問題。

## 跨資產

股市走強進一步推升實質殖利率，也降低即時避險需求。S&P 500上漲0.7920%，Nasdaq 100上漲1.6846%，費城半導體指數大漲3.9191%。VIX下跌6.7989%至16.45。漲勢雖集中於科技及晶片類股，大盤普遍上揚仍顯示市場將勞動市場韌性解讀為企業獲利信心，而非經濟即將失速。

能源價格則朝有利債券存續期間的方向發展，使風險偏好訊號更為複雜。市場期待美國與伊朗達成持久協議，實體供給溢價因而下降。WTI下跌1.7668%至$69.50，Brent下跌0.3144%至$72.92，兩者在1個月內均下跌逾20%。單日及月度跌幅帶動歐洲通膨降溫，也限制美國損益兩平通膨率升幅，但仍不足以抵銷勞動數據與資產價格走強所帶來的實質殖利率壓力。

美元與黃金幾乎未反映系統性避險需求。美元指數僅上漲0.0791%至101.19，當日外部流動性衝擊有限，但1個月內仍上漲2.3051%。黃金幾乎持平於$4,022.90，月內則下跌11.7882%。金價穩定、波動率下降及股市上漲同時出現，顯示美債賣壓較接近成長與政策重新定價，而非地緣政治通膨衝擊捲土重來。

科技業的跨資產訊號仍存在內部張力。半導體類股單季漲幅創新高，支撐股市、招聘預期與資本支出，並抬高實質利率底線。同一波投資週期也需要大量、且可能為長天期的融資，用於技術上可能迅速過時的資產。因此，股市走強可以和美債殖利率上升、債權人審查趨嚴同時出現。油價下跌緩和名目通膨壓力，卻未解答AI支出能否持續推升生產力與獲利，並支應相關債務。

## 市場前瞻意義

7月1日至2日公布的美國勞動、經濟活動及物價數據，是檢驗週二實質殖利率升勢的最近一組事件。ADP就業數據於週三美東時間上午8:15公布，接著是上午9:45的製造業PMI終值，以及上午10:00的ISM製造業指數與營建支出；因假期提前公布的非農就業報告及初領失業救濟金人數，則於週四上午8:30公布。若招聘持穩或增強、薪資堅挺，投入價格又維持高檔，將證實職缺及德州服務業數據反映廣泛的經濟韌性，並推升2年至10年期實質殖利率及聯準會進一步維持限制性政策的預期。若就業轉弱，同時訂單與價格走軟，則會挑戰此一解讀，使先前中段債券的漲勢恢復。週四下午2:00提前收盤，市場反應將集中在較短的流動性窗口，因此除了數據公布後的初步變動，也須觀察殖利率曲線調整的幅度與持續性。

7月1日中歐夏令時間上午11:00公布的歐元區初值通膨，將決定各國通膨降溫是否已成為全區政策訊號。若整體通膨率較5月的3.2%普遍放緩，服務通膨維持受控，油價也守在較低區間，將證實法國、德國及義大利的數據確實反映能源衝擊消退。最敏感的傳導管道包括德國公債前端殖利率、歐元區通膨補償及美債損益兩平通膨率；輸入成本壓力下降，也有利石油進口國的新興市場主權債。若服務通膨僵固、能源價格反彈，或美國與伊朗停火再次受阻，將重新引發Lane與Nagel所強調的成本後續傳導疑慮，挑戰Kazaks與Rehn認為升息迫切性下降的看法。即使當前原油價格仍遠低於戰時高點，全球政策利率底線仍可能上升。

美國季底過後，主權債承接焦點將轉向日本。規模約¥2.6兆的新發10年期日本公債預定於7月2日標售，隨後約¥6,000億的30年期公債將於7月7日標售。美國7月1日標售17週期國庫券，7月2日則各標售$850億的4週期與8週期國庫券，將在美國獨立紀念日假期前後同步檢驗現金需求。若最終投資人踴躍參與，長天期日本公債殖利率也保持穩定，將顯示週二的2年期需求可延伸至前端以外，並挑戰財政擴張與日圓疲弱必然使日本殖利率曲線持續趨陡的看法。若需求疲弱或超長端再度下跌，則會證實日本投資組合配置正透過期限溢價推升全球殖利率。美國方面，若7月2日交割有序且國庫券殖利率穩定，局部6週期壓力可望化解；若國庫券突然走弱或交易商承接比例上升，資產負債表限制將再度成為焦點，並威脅縮短交易時段內的附息債市場流動性。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The June 30 close broadened the prior session’s front-led repricing into a selloff across the Treasury curve. The 10-year yield finished at 4.44%, up 6 basis points, as a rise in its real yield to 2.20% accounted for 4 basis points of the move. The central interpretation changed at the margin: long-duration demand and easing energy pressure no longer insulated intermediate Treasuries from evidence of resilient labor demand, firmer consumer confidence and powerful equity risk appetite. Inflation compensation also rose, so the close carried both a higher real-rate hurdle and a modest restoration of inflation risk.

US data supplied the 1st transmission channel. May job openings exceeded expectations and edged above April’s revised level, suggesting that labor demand had not weakened decisively. Consumer confidence improved, even though households’ assessment of the job market deteriorated. A Texas services survey paired faster revenue and employment with higher input costs, wages and selling prices. That combination gave the Federal Reserve room to remain restrictive and encouraged renewed expectations of tightening later in the year. Softer house prices and the uneven confidence details prevented the data from becoming a clean acceleration signal.

Global duration delivered a strong counterpoint without rescuing Treasuries. Lower oil helped inflation slow more than expected in Germany and France, reducing the urgency for consecutive ECB increases. Japan moved in the opposite direction: strong demand at a 2-year auction coincided with a sharp super-long selloff as fiscal expansion, a deeply weak yen and doubts about the pace of BOJ normalization raised long-run inflation and supply compensation. The resulting cross-market message was disinflation at the energy margin alongside persistent pressure on real rates and sovereign term premium.

Credit remained accessible in aggregate, yet financing outcomes became more selective. Japanese companies completed a record quarter of foreign-currency issuance, and emerging-market international bond sales reached a H1 record. Sable Offshore’s sharply downsized leveraged loan, China’s restrictions on high-cost offshore borrowing and growing concern about the maturity mismatch in AI debt showed where that access was weakest. The close therefore represented a risk-on, higher-real-yield session with functioning primary markets, rather than a generalized withdrawal of liquidity. Its main unresolved issue is whether cheaper energy can keep inflation expectations contained when labor demand, capital spending and asset prices remain firm.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

Treasury losses were broad and concentrated most heavily around the benchmark maturity. The 2-year yield rose 4 basis points to 4.14%, the 5-year increased 5 to 4.19%, the 10-year climbed 6 to 4.44%, and the 30-year added 5 to 4.91%. This replaced Monday’s mild bear flattening with a modest bear steepening through 10 years. Policy restraint still mattered at the front, but stronger growth-sensitive pricing and reduced demand for protection extended the adjustment into the belly and long end.

Curve slopes captured that change in leadership. The 2s10s spread widened 2 basis points to 30, and 2s30s widened 1 to 77. The 5-year remained rich against its wings: the 2s5s10s butterfly held at -20. The 2s10s30s butterfly rose 3 basis points to -17 as the 10-year underperformed the average of the front end and long bond. Those moves were measured, yet they show that the session was more than a mechanical reversal in the 2-year sector.

The longer comparison still separated near-term policy pressure from distant duration relief. Over 1 month, the 2-year yield was 16 basis points higher and the 5-year 6 higher, whereas the 10-year was 1 basis point lower and the 30-year 8 lower. June’s oil retreat and lower inflation expectations preserved gains at longer maturities, even as the hawkish Fed shift lifted the front. Tuesday’s selloff narrowed that divergence without eliminating it. Investors raised the cost of holding duration for the day while retaining a substantially different monthly judgment about the policy path and the far-end clearing rate.

Inflation-linked markets divided the 6-basis-point rise in the nominal 10-year yield between real and inflation components. The 10-year real yield rose 4 basis points to 2.20%, and the breakeven increased 2 to 2.24%. 5-year real yields gained 3 basis points to 1.93%, 7-year real yields rose 4 to 2.06%, and 20- and 30-year real yields each added 5, to 2.54% and 2.73%. The parallel increase in real compensation indicates that the nominal selloff was rooted in a higher growth and policy hurdle, with a smaller contribution from inflation risk.

May job openings provided the clearest same-session catalyst. Available positions rose to 7.59 million, slightly above April’s revised level and above expectations. The release suggested stable labor demand after the recent pickup in payroll growth and weighed on Treasuries. Conference Board confidence also edged higher in June, reinforcing resilience in aggregate demand. Its labor-market details were less reassuring: consumers’ assessment of employment conditions deteriorated and they expected little improvement. The data therefore weakened the case for imminent policy relief without establishing a uniformly stronger labor market.

Regional and housing data kept the Fed signal two-sided. The Dallas Fed’s Texas services revenue index rose to 9.8 from 5.0, employment to 8.1 from -3.2, and general business activity to 2.9 from -7.7. Input prices climbed to 36.5 from 29.7, wages and benefits to 15.3 from 6.2, and selling prices to 7.7 from 5.0. Against that firmer activity-and-cost mix, the FHFA house-price index fell 0.1% in April and annual appreciation slowed to 2.0%, tempering the housing-inflation and collateral signal.

Expectations for at least 1 Fed increase in H2 had persisted through the collapse in oil from its wartime peak, and Tuesday’s releases strengthened that restrictive interpretation. The curve did not price a simple revival of the energy shock: crude fell on the day and most of the 10-year move came from real yield. The combination instead suggested that policy may need to stay tight because labor demand and spending have remained resilient, with AI-related investment adding another possible demand and inflation channel. Softer housing and weaker consumer labor perceptions remain credible competing evidence.

The bill curve showed localized quarter-end pressure rather than a uniform cash squeeze. The 4-week coupon-equivalent yield fell 2 basis points to 3.67%, 6 weeks rose 5 to 3.73%, and 8 weeks held at 3.73%. 13- and 17-week yields were unchanged at 3.83% and 3.88%, while 26 and 52 weeks each added 1 basis point, to 3.98% and 3.97%. The sharpest daily move sat at 6 weeks, where new supply and the holiday funding window concentrated attention.

Treasury’s $80.000 billion 42-day bill auction stopped at a 3.655% high rate with a 2.71 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders took 69.01% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders 4.96%, and dealers 26.03%; 54.61% was allotted at the high. The July 2 issue and settlement date keeps Tuesday’s bidding outcome separate from the coming cash transfer. The sale established absorption across quarter-end, though the simultaneous rise in the 6-week cash yield left the funding signal less uniformly easy than the shortest bill suggested.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Listed credit returns reflected the Treasury selloff more clearly in higher-grade duration than in lower-quality risk. LQD fell 0.5743%, while HYG declined 0.0500% and JNK slipped 0.0311%. Strong equities and lower volatility helped speculative-grade funds stay near flat, even as the rise in benchmark yields pulled down the longer-duration investment-grade fund. The pattern described stable broad risk appetite with a duration drag, leaving issuer terms and funding structures to reveal where credit access was genuinely constrained.

Japanese issuers demonstrated exceptional access to dollar markets. Mizuho Financial Group and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group priced almost $10 billion of debt at the start of the week, lifting quarterly foreign-currency issuance by Japanese companies to about $54 billion. That total was more than 80% above a year earlier and Q1 above $50 billion in data back to 1999. Panasonic began another dollar offering Tuesday. A weak yen increases the domestic proceeds available after swapping funds back, while higher local rates make offshore financing more relevant for acquisitions and expansion.

Sable Offshore exposed the opposite end of the absorption spectrum. Limited demand for a 15% fixed-rate leveraged loan led its size to be cut from an original $1 billion to $675 million, despite an offer price of 97 cents and a short 2.5-year maturity. The company also sought $400 million through equity and convertible notes, with the converts offering a coupon of as much as 6.5% and a 30% to 35% conversion premium. Its shares fell as much as 55%, showing the dilution and refinancing cost imposed by a near-term liability.

The Sable financing was intended to repay an Exxon Mobil term loan whose maturity had already required a $30 million extension payment; the revised extension was set to run through July 31. Amortization sweeteners could reduce the loan balance over its life, but litigation around the company’s restarted California offshore operations still complicated cash-flow visibility. Strong general demand in leveraged finance did not translate into full absorption for a borrower combining execution risk, compressed timing and an unusually high coupon.

China tightened the boundary around expensive offshore refinancing. The National Development and Reform Commission asked selected bankers to avoid underwriting offshore yuan bonds yielding above 4% and dollar bonds above 5%, particularly for local-government financing vehicles. LGFVs had about $117 billion of offshore bonds outstanding, and Chinese companies faced roughly $71 billion of maturities during the rest of 2026, followed by a wall above $130 billion next year. Some quotas had been reduced by 10% to 20%, forcing at least 1 state-owned borrower toward costlier short-term bank funding.

Private markets showed a related liquidity fault line. Len Tannenbaum was seeking capital for a new fund as redemption requests rose across major alternative managers and liquidity drained from parts of the $1.8 trillion private-credit market. He identified smaller software companies as especially vulnerable to refinancing trouble within a year, even as lower-middle-market borrowers with real cash flow retained access. The divergence suggests that a broad pool of private capital can coexist with tighter covenants and higher spreads where AI disruption has weakened earnings visibility.

AI financing added a duration mismatch to the credit story. IMF capital-markets director Tobias Adrian focused on hyperscalers issuing medium- and long-term debt to fund chips and other physical assets that may become obsolete much faster. Strong profitability and earnings delivery have so far distinguished the boom from a generalized valuation bubble. The credit consequence is still material: record technology equity performance can support financing today while large future capital needs increase supply and leave long-dated creditors exposed if monetization disappoints.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

European inflation data strengthened the energy-disinflation channel. German inflation slowed to 2.4% in June from 2.7%, below the 2.5% median estimate. France fell to 2.0% from 2.8%, against an expected 2.3%, and Italy moderated to 3.1% when economists had expected no change. Spain’s earlier 3.6% reading remained the main national counterexample. The breadth of the declines reduced the immediate need for another ECB increase and helped explain why lower oil did not generate a larger rise in US breakevens.

ECB officials kept the policy consequence conditional on pass-through. Martins Kazaks said the urgency of consecutive moves had decreased significantly after peace efforts lowered energy prices, while Olli Rehn saw no major second-round effects and described inflation expectations as anchored. Chief Economist Philip Lane remained focused on how 4 months of higher energy costs might enter food and services. The June rate increase, the first since 2023, left the policy rate at 2.25%; softer national prints shifted the debate toward patience without resolving the pipeline risk.

The German labor release reinforced the case for patience. Seasonally adjusted unemployment fell by only 1,000 in June, and the BA-X labor-demand index held at 103. Social-insurance employment was 71,000 below a year earlier in the latest estimate. Weak labor demand limited the scope for energy costs to create a wage-price loop, even though headline inflation remained above target. European duration therefore received support from both lower current energy inflation and a subdued labor backdrop, with services and food pass-through still the limiting condition.

UK data offered a similar split between resilient output and weaker household demand. Q1 real GDP growth was unrevised at 0.6%, led by a 0.8% rise in services. Real household disposable income per head fell 0.8%, and the saving ratio dropped to 8.9% from 9.6%. The underlying current-account deficit narrowed to £15.1 billion, or 1.9% of GDP, as a smaller primary-income deficit outweighed a wider trade gap. Growth prevented a pure duration rally, while household income and external-balance improvement reduced separate gilt risk channels.

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey emphasized that lower oil had reopened policy flexibility. Before the war, pricing for 2 reductions from the 3.75% policy rate had been reasonable in his view. Crude had since fallen below $80 after exceeding $110, below the path embedded in the BOE’s April forecast. Bailey still expected inflation to rise from 2.8% to around 3.2% later in the year, yet he stressed weak growth and the medium-term horizon. Gilts consequently faced less urgency from energy without receiving a clear near-term easing commitment.

Japan supplied the session’s strongest sovereign-duration counterforce. The 30-year JGB yield rose 11 basis points to 3.94%, and the 20-year climbed 9 to 3.64%. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s plan to mobilize more than ¥370 trillion of public and private investment through fiscal 2040 raised concern about future supply and fiscal sustainability. USD/JPY moving above 162 intensified the pressure by highlighting imported inflation and doubts that a government preference for easy policy would allow the BOJ to normalize quickly enough.

The front end told a different Japanese story. The 2-year auction drew a 4.82 bid-to-cover ratio, up from 3.70 at the previous sale and above the 3.74 12-month average. Its tail narrowed to 0.005 from 0.02, and the 2-year yield fell 1.5 basis points after the result. Demand reflected elevated front-end yields and expectations of a cautious BOJ. That strength sharpened the curve split because it did little to resolve long-end fiscal and inflation risk.

Domestic buyer capacity offered a partial long-end stabilizer. Meiji Yasuda planned more than ¥2 trillion of super-long JGB purchases in the fiscal year ending March 2027, double its earlier plan, after the rise in yields. A new BOJ board member appointed by Takaichi also said an inflationary norm was not yet firmly established, reinforcing expectations of gradual normalization. After the New York close, the IMF separately urged New Zealand’s central bank to lift its 2.25% rate toward a neutral level centered near 3% by year-end, adding a later Asia-Pacific tightening signal for the next global session.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Broad emerging-market debt weakened as US real yields rose. EMB fell 0.3925%, while the Dollar Index was nearly flat on the day. The aggregate move was mild relative to the Treasury selloff, and primary access remained exceptionally strong. Emerging-market sovereigns and companies sold a record $450 billion of dollar- and euro-denominated bonds in H1, 15% more than a year earlier, as spreads over Treasuries narrowed to 154 basis points, their tightest since 2007.

That issuance strength creates a demanding valuation backdrop. Mexico, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Poland, Turkey and Brazil each raised more than $10 billion, and EM dollar debt returned 2.1% during H1, 3 times the Treasury gain. A large global buyer base helped borrowers bring forward funding during tight spreads. Tuesday’s rise in US yields shows the vulnerability on the other side: debt-service costs and secondary performance can deteriorate even when the broad dollar index is calm.

Ethiopia made tangible progress from the legal and coordination stalemate visible at prior closes. A committee representing about 45% of its 2024 noteholders confirmed a tentative agreement on key restructuring terms, and the defaulted securities extended gains to 109.17 cents. The agreement softened the immediate enforcement risk following the 2023 missed coupon. Creditors’ criticism of the IMF’s dual role as senior lender and debt-sustainability arbiter kept Common Framework governance unresolved, so better recovery expectations did not close the process-risk question.

Local policy credibility continued to draw capital into selected Asian sovereigns. Foreign investors bought a net $1.2 billion of Indonesian government bonds through June 26, the strongest monthly pace in more than a year, after Bank Indonesia tightened unexpectedly to support the rupiah. The 10-year yield stood at 7.12%, down from 7.47% earlier in June. India received a record $4.2 billion into index-eligible government debt as lower oil eased its import bill, though a weak monsoon remained a potential food-inflation constraint.

Latin American markets rewarded decisive policy action and disinflation selectively. Colombia raised its policy rate by 75 basis points to 12% after a court ended the government’s ability to obstruct central-bank meetings; bonds and the currency rallied as the result exceeded most forecasts. Poland’s inflation fell to 2.5% from 3.1%, below the 2.7% median estimate, sending its benchmark 10-year yield to the lowest since early March even as the zloty weakened. Chile’s 1-year breakeven had dropped more than 100 basis points over the month to 2.19%, concentrating easing expectations at the short end.

South Africa remained on the inflation-sensitive side of that divide. 2-year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 3.9% from 3.6%, above the central bank’s 3% target, and forward-rate agreements priced an 88% chance of a quarter-point increase. The contrast with Poland and Chile shows how the retreat in global oil has not delivered a uniform local-rate outcome. Domestic expectations, food risks and institutional reaction functions still determine whether cheaper energy becomes lower sovereign funding costs.

China’s official June surveys supplied a mixed regional demand signal. Manufacturing returned to expansion at 50.3, with production at 51.4 and new orders at 51.2, but employment fell to 48.5 and the small-firm index to 48.2. Non-manufacturing activity held at 50.2, while construction remained in contraction at 49.0. The figures supported commodity and export demand at the margin without erasing stress among smaller borrowers, which reinforces the refinancing concern created by tighter offshore issuance rules for LGFVs.

Foreign allocation showed that the improvement extended beyond equities and
the rupee. Overseas investors added a record 398 billion rupees of
index-eligible Indian government bonds during June after New Delhi removed the
tax on government debt, even as they withdrew $3.1 billion from equities. The
bond inflow provided a direct local-duration demand channel and helped the rupee
recover from the prior month's record low near 97 per dollar. Lower oil and the
tax change improved access, while weak-monsoon risk still left food inflation
and the RBI reaction as limits on the trade.

A later post-close account added Venezuela to the debt-management risk list. Twin earthquakes had caused an estimated $6.7 billion of direct damage and bonds were falling as investors weighed the fiscal cost against an already difficult restructuring. Its timing prevents that development from explaining the completed US session. It nevertheless adds a next-session sovereign loss-absorption problem in which disaster spending, scarce external liquidity and existing creditor negotiations interact.

## Cross asset

Equities reinforced the rise in real yields and the reduction in immediate haven demand. The S&P 500 gained 0.7920%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.6846%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 3.9191%. The VIX fell 6.7989% to 16.45. The leadership was concentrated in technology and chips, but the broad advance still supported the interpretation that labor resilience was translating into earnings confidence rather than an imminent growth break.

Energy complicated that risk-on message in a duration-friendly direction. WTI fell 1.7668% to $69.50 and Brent slipped 0.3144% to $72.92 as hopes for a durable US-Iran settlement reduced the physical-supply premium. Both contracts were down more than 20% over 1 month. The daily and monthly declines helped European inflation cool and limited the rise in US breakevens, yet they were insufficient to offset the real-yield pressure generated by labor data and strong asset prices.

The dollar and gold showed little demand for systemic protection. The Dollar Index rose only 0.0791% to 101.19, leaving the daily external-liquidity impulse small even though it remained 2.3051% higher over 1 month. Gold was almost unchanged at $4,022.90 and stood 11.7882% lower over the month. Stable bullion alongside falling volatility and rising equities made the Treasury selloff look more like a growth-and-policy repricing than a renewed geopolitical inflation shock.

Technology’s cross-asset signal remained internally tense. A record quarterly semiconductor advance supported equities, hiring expectations and capital spending, all of which raise the real-rate floor. The same investment cycle requires large and potentially long-dated financing for assets exposed to rapid obsolescence. Equity strength can therefore coexist with rising Treasury yields and greater creditor scrutiny. Lower oil eased the nominal inflation channel, but it did not settle whether AI expenditure will sustain productivity and earnings strongly enough to service the debt created around it.

## Forward Market Significance

The US labor, activity and price sequence on July 1 and July 2 is the nearest test of Tuesday’s real-yield selloff. ADP employment arrives at 8:15 a.m. ET Wednesday, followed by final manufacturing PMI at 9:45 and ISM manufacturing plus construction spending at 10:00; the holiday-advanced payroll report and initial claims follow at 8:30 Thursday. Stable or stronger hiring, firm wages and another elevated input-price reading would confirm that the JOLTS and Texas services signals describe broad resilience, transmitting through 2- to 10-year real yields and expectations of further Fed restraint. Weaker employment paired with softer orders and prices would challenge that interpretation and restore the prior belly-duration relief. Thursday’s 2:00 p.m. early close concentrates the reaction in a shorter liquidity window, so depth and persistence of the curve move matter alongside the initial release response.

Euro-area flash inflation at 11:00 a.m. CEST on July 1 determines whether national disinflation has become an area-wide policy signal. A broad slowdown from May’s 3.2% headline rate, especially alongside contained services inflation and oil holding near its lower range, would confirm that France, Germany and Italy are capturing a genuine retreat in the energy shock. The sensitive channels are front-end Bund yields, euro inflation compensation and Treasury breakevens, with lower imported-cost pressure also helping oil-importing EM sovereigns. Sticky services, a rebound in energy or renewed disruption around the US-Iran ceasefire would reopen the pipeline concern emphasized by Lane and Nagel, challenge the reduced urgency expressed by Kazaks and Rehn, and raise the global policy floor even if current crude prices remain well below their wartime peak.

Sovereign absorption shifts to Japan after the US quarter turn. The new roughly ¥2.6 trillion 10-year JGB auction is due July 2, followed by an approximately ¥600 billion 30-year sale on July 7; US 17-week bills on July 1 and the paired $85 billion 4- and 8-week auctions on July 2 add a parallel cash-demand check around the Independence Day schedule. Strong end-investor participation and stable long JGB yields would show that Tuesday’s 2-year demand can extend beyond the front end, challenging the view that fiscal expansion and yen weakness require a persistently steeper Japanese curve. Weak demand or renewed super-long cheapening would confirm a higher global term-premium channel through Japanese portfolio allocation. In the US, orderly July 2 settlement and stable bill yields would resolve the localized 6-week pressure; abrupt cheapening or heavier dealer absorption would reopen the balance-sheet constraint and threaten coupon-market liquidity during the shortened session.
